Shelf will search for folders it hid but no longer tracks, then restore every folder in the list. Anything it cannot reach is reported at the end and left alone.
Shelf hides folders from your gallery and file manager, then disguises itself as an ordinary app. This takes a minute, and everything here can be changed later.
Shelf randomizes file names and protects headers for fast hiding, not whole files. It stops ordinary browsing and previews, not forensic recovery by someone determined with a computer.
This is the name and icon Shelf wears on your home screen. Each one is a working app in its own right.
How you will get back in
Five taps in the top-right corner always open the credential prompt. Choose a second, quieter gesture as well.
Renaming works everywhere and needs no permission. Root and all-files access hide folders more thoroughly, if this phone offers them.
Optional, and the strongest option without root. It lets Shelf move a folder into hidden storage under a random name — instantly, whatever its size, and it survives uninstalling the app.
Granting this puts “All files access” in Shelf\'s entry in Android\'s permission settings, which is a hint about what the app really does. Without it, folders are hidden by renaming instead.
A quiet notification, carrying your disguise\'s name, with one action that closes the private space and puts every folder back out of sight.
Optional. You can turn this on later in Settings.
4 to 12 digits. This opens your real private space.
There is no way to reset this PIN. Nothing leaves your device, so nobody can recover it for you.
